affectedCopies: The reversible restaurant demo loader now writes the existing HospitalityResource, StaffingShift, StaffingAssignment, StaffingResourceLink, HospitalityServiceTurn, HospitalityServiceTurnEvent, HospitalityCapacityAllocation, and StorefrontBooking authorities instead of a parallel fixture store.
The Workspace host stand and customer-safe availability projection continue to read the canonical restaurant floor projection; no new projection copy is persisted.
Existing real restaurant rows are excluded. The fleet backfill matches only platform-owned demo-restaurant provider and booking references.

No schema field or relationship is added: serviceArea, blockedReason, attributes, staffingAssignmentId, demandRef, and dietaryNotes are pre-existing Prisma authorities. The migration contains data repair only.

Demo identifiers are already globally unique in the canonical schema (ServiceProvider.providerId, StorefrontBooking.bookingRef, StaffingShift.shiftId, StaffingAssignment.assignmentId, HospitalityServiceTurn.turnId, and allocationId). That invariant admits at most one matching canonical restaurant demo corpus and prevents cross-organization conflict fall-through.

migration.name: 20260808183000_repair_restaurant_demo_floor + 20260808184500_minimize_restaurant_demo_guest_data
migration.backfill: Data-only and demo-scoped. The first migration converts the existing reversible demo-restaurant legacy table rows into named service areas with realistic capacities and validated shapes, refreshes seven demo bookings into a bounded busy shift, publishes two demo staffing sections, and creates stable service turns/allocations. The immediately following corrective migration clears dietaryNotes on those exact demo bookings, and the final loader code seeds no guest-sensitive note text. Prior active demo allocations transition to released with a reason; no capacity history is deleted. Real resources, bookings, staffing, layouts, and customer data are untouched. Demo rows remain removable through the existing reversible demo teardown; retained allocation history is demo-only operational evidence with no guest note payload.
